F01.name: Mixed date formats
F01.summary: Each document uses its own date convention (2026-03-31, 31/03/2026, 31-Mar-26, March 2026, Q1 FY26); hand-edited rows drift from their file's house style.
F01.handling: Parse with a multi-format date parser and normalise to ISO-8601 at ingestion; resolve dd/mm vs mm/dd against the file's dominant style and keep the raw string in metadata.

F02.name: Mixed currency notation
F02.summary: The same amount appears as 1200000, "1,200,000", "S$1.2M", "1200k" and "1,200,000 SGD"; negatives as -45000 and (45,000).
F02.handling: Strip symbols/separators and expand k/M suffixes to a numeric value plus a currency code; read parenthesised numbers as negative.

F03.name: Inconsistent status vocabulary
F03.summary: RAG and progress states are spelled every way a human would type them: Green / GREEN / On Track / G, Amber / At Risk / Yellow, Complete / Completed / DONE / done.
F03.handling: Map to a controlled vocabulary with a case-insensitive synonym table; surface unmapped values rather than silently dropping them.

F04.name: Header naming drift
F04.summary: The same concept is headed differently across files and within one header row (Owner / Risk Owner / Accountable, Date Raised / raised_date).
F04.handling: Resolve headers through a synonym map to canonical field names; match case-insensitively after stripping punctuation and spaces.

F05.name: Whitespace, casing and filename drift
F05.summary: Leading/trailing and doubled spaces in cells, the project name cased three ways, and filenames following three different conventions.
F05.handling: Strip and collapse whitespace on ingestion; casefold before matching entity names; never derive metadata from the filename alone.

F06.name: Mixed scale and percentage notation
F06.summary: Likelihood is 'High' in one row, '4' in another and '80%' in a third; completion shows as 0.35, 35% and '35 pct'.
F06.handling: Detect ordinal-vs-numeric-vs-percentage per value and convert to one scale; record the interpretation so an answer can cite the raw form.

F07.name: Decimal and thousands separator drift
F07.summary: One locale-confused export row writes 1.250,00 and another 1 250, alongside the file's normal 1,250.00.
F07.handling: Sniff the separator per value (last separator wins as decimal) instead of a global locale assumption; quarantine what stays ambiguous.

F08.name: UTF-8 BOM and non-ASCII text
F08.summary: A CSV starts with a BOM and carries en-dashes, curly quotes and accented vendor names.
F08.handling: Open CSVs as utf-8-sig and keep text as Unicode; normalise dashes and quotes only for matching, not for display.

F09.name: Mixed line endings
F09.summary: One CSV is written with CRLF line endings and a trailing blank line, as exported from a Windows finance tool.
F09.handling: Read with universal newlines and drop empty trailing records.

F10.name: Repeated page furniture in PDFs
F10.summary: Every PDF page repeats a confidentiality banner, project code and 'Page x of y', which lands in the middle of extracted text.
F10.handling: Strip repeated header/footer lines during PDF extraction (drop lines that recur on most pages) before chunking, so chunks stay clean.

M01.name: Blank required fields
M01.summary: A milestone with no owner, a risk with no review date, a cost line with no vendor - cells simply left empty.
M01.handling: Treat empty as unknown rather than zero; keep the row, flag the gap, and say the field is missing rather than inventing a value.

M02.name: Inconsistent null tokens
M02.summary: Absent values are written as TBD, N/A, n/a, -, tbc, unknown and ??? in the same column.
M02.handling: Normalise a null-token list to a real null at ingestion, case-insensitively, so counts and aggregates don't treat 'N/A' as a value.

M03.name: Risk recorded without mitigation
M03.summary: At least one high-scoring risk has an empty mitigation/action cell.
M03.handling: Surface it as an explicit gap ('no mitigation recorded') - a question about mitigations must not silently skip the row.

M04.name: Spreadsheet title rows and merged cells
M04.summary: The workbook opens with a merged title banner and an export stamp above the real header row, so row 1 is not the header.
M04.handling: Detect the header row by scanning for the first row that looks like field names; unmerge and forward-fill merged cells before parsing.

M05.name: Ragged CSV row
M05.summary: One free-text field contains an unquoted comma, so that row parses with one column too many.
M05.handling: Parse leniently and repair rows whose field count is off by one by re-joining the overflow into the free-text column; log the repair.

M06.name: Numbers stored as text
M06.summary: Some spreadsheet amounts are strings (" 1,200,000 ", "1.2m") rather than numeric cells.
M06.handling: Coerce per cell rather than trusting the column type; keep the raw string when coercion fails instead of dropping the row.

M07.name: Placeholder and truncated text
M07.summary: Notes read 'see attached', 'per last month', '???' or stop mid-sentence.
M07.handling: Treat placeholder phrases as non-answers; never quote them as the substance of a mitigation or decision.

M08.name: Omitted report section
M08.summary: One status report has no budget section at all - the author ran out of time that month.
M08.handling: Answer from the period that does report it and say the section is absent, rather than assuming the figure is unchanged or zero.

M09.name: Trailing empty rows and columns
M09.summary: The sheet's used range extends past the data with blank rows and a stray empty column.
M09.handling: Trim wholly empty rows/columns after reading the used range so row counts and aggregates are right.

M10.name: Embedded total row
M10.summary: A 'TOTAL' row sits inside the data rows of the export, not in a separate summary block.
M10.handling: Detect and exclude label rows (TOTAL/Subtotal/Grand Total) before aggregating, or the numbers double-count.
